hunts.label: Saturday, Nov 14
hunts.subtitle: The front blew the sky clean. Sit in the lee, let the gusts pass, and let the squirrels come to you.

rules.title: Rules for this hunt
items: No clock change before this hunt. The next one is Sunday Mar 14, 2027 (spring forward).
**Bear season opens today** (Nov 14 to 22). You do not hunt bear, but other hunters may be out. Deer gun season is still open for them: stay in orange.
**Saturday is a crow day** (Wed, Fri, Sat only). Dove segment 2 and snipe are open. Quail opens next Saturday, Nov 21.
rules.note: Small game focus for the rest of the season. Deer: tag filled. Do not shoot a deer.

items: 9 am: mid-40s (assumption). The afternoon high is near **55F**.
Wind: **NW 6 to 9 mph, gusts to 15** overnight. Saturday morning wind was not listed; expect it to ease (assumption).
Sky: partly cloudy overnight, then **sunny**. No rain in the forecast.
Moon: **waxing crescent, about 29 percent**. It sets in the evening, so the morning is dark.
conditions.meaning: Assumption: a cool, clear morning after a front means squirrels stay tucked in until the sun reaches the trunks, and gusts keep them low in the canopy. Expect the best squirrel and rabbit movement from about 7:00 to 9:00, when the wind eases and the sun warms the east faces.
conditions.hours_note: No hour-by-hour table was available for the hunt morning, so the hourly chart is left out. Temperatures above are estimates from the daily forecast.

in_season.tip: Feed trees on sunlit trunks after 7:00.
Sunny edges of thick cover and the feed bins area.
Last ones heading to dens at first light.
Opportunity from the sit. Shots north only.
Opportunity only. HIP and plug required. Never toward the field SE.
Check the swamp mud on the walk. HIP and plug required.
Open, but skipped today. Ducks need steel shot, HIP, federal stamp, and state waterfowl privilege.

in_season: Quail opens Nov 21. Woodcock opens Dec 10.
Deer: tag filled for the season. Do not shoot a deer.
Bear and bobcat are open. You do not hunt them. Stay aware near the swamp.

plan.title: Hardwood Pocket Seat
plan.why: You are hunting food, so sit where squirrels eat. Find the spot on the loop trail where holly and one or two oaks or hickories stand close together, with cut hulls, nut bits, or holly skins on the ground. Put your back to a wide pine on the **south** edge of that pocket and face **N to NE**. The sun comes up behind your right shoulder and lights the trunks in front of you. The NW wind crosses you from the left, and the pines to your west break the gusts. Squirrels will hear you before they smell you, so sit still. Every shot goes north, through the hardwoods, with trunks and ground behind.

steps.text: Leave the yard by the main trail. Red light only. Walk 20 steps, stop 10 seconds, repeat. Gun unloaded.
Turn onto the loop trail and find the hardwood pocket. Step 15 yards off the trail to the pine. Sit, face N to NE, load #4, plug in. Red light off.
Legal light. Do not move. Scan the trunks 20 to 40 yards out, from NW round to E. Listen for cuttings falling and claws on bark.
Sunrise. Watch the sunlit faces of the trunks. Do the skill-of-the-week scan (see below) while you wait.
Peak squirrel time begins as the wind eases. Use the leaf-scratch call once, then stay still for 10 minutes.
Still-hunt slowly NW into the wind along the loop to the main trail. 3 steps, 20 seconds still. Shots N only.
Walk the main trail to the Junction and look at the swamp-edge pines in full sun. Crow check: listen for calls overhead.
Loop to the feed bins. Walk the sunny edge of the thick cover for rabbit. Shoot N or W only; never toward the field SE.
Unload at the bins. Walk out by the main trail. Do the land task on the way.

items: **In the gun: #4** (plug in, 3 shells max). Good for squirrel to 35 yards.
**Right pocket: #7.5** for dove, crow, snipe, or a close rabbit.
**Slugs: zipped in a separate pocket.** Bear defense only.
**.22 LR (optional):** head shots on still squirrels only, with a trunk or the ground behind the squirrel.
warnings: Never shoot a deer with birdshot. Not with #4, not with #7.5.
Swap shells in the open with the muzzle north. Count every shell in and out.
Gusts shake dead limbs loose. Do not sit under snags or leaning dead pines.

animals.name: Gray squirrel and fox squirrel
paragraphs: The most common game on the property. Grays work the hardwoods, holly, and swamp edge. A fox squirrel, bigger and orange-brown, may show in the open pines.
After a cold front they stay in the nest until the sun finds the trunks. Gusts push them low and tight to the bark. Expect the best hour from 7:15 to 8:30.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 at 20 to 35 yards. Aim at the head and front shoulders.
With the .22: head only, with wood or ground behind the squirrel.
After the shot, wait 10 minutes. Others freeze, then move again.
details.note: Mark the fall against a trunk or stump before you move.

details.title: Call: leaf scratch
steps: Reach down and rake dry leaves with your fingers.
Make 3 or 4 short scratches, pause 2 seconds, then 3 or 4 more.
Stop for 10 minutes. Watch for a head or tail flick.
It sounds like a squirrel digging a nut. Use it from the seat only.

after: Tip: in gusts, look for the tail edge moving against the wind, not with the branches.
Tip: a squirrel that circles the trunk away from you will come back around if you stay still for 2 minutes.

animals.name: Rabbit
paragraphs: Cottontails use the thick edges near the feed bins and the pine-holly thickets.
On a cool sunny morning they sit at the first warm edge of cover and trust their color.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 or #7.5 at 15 to 25 yards. Aim at the head and front shoulders.
Shoot only with the ground behind the rabbit.
Never shoot toward the south line or the field SE.

details.title: Technique: edge walk
steps: Walk the sunny edge of a thicket slowly, into the wind.
Look for the round black eye and the ear line, not the whole body.
Stop 15 yards short. Wait 30 seconds. A rabbit that thinks it is seen will run.

after: Tip: wear gloves to clean rabbits. Discard any rabbit with white spots on the liver.

animals.name: Raccoon and opossum
paragraphs: Both feed at night along the swamp and around the feed bins. At first light the last ones head for hollow trees and root dens.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 to the head at 20 yards or less.
Approach from behind. Touch the eye with a stick to confirm it is dead. Opossums play dead.
details.note: Wear gloves. Rabies is possible in raccoons.

after: Tip: hair on the edge of a feed bin means one rubbed past in the night.

animals.name: Crow
paragraphs: Crows roost off the property and fly over to feed. Saturday is a legal day. After a front they fly early and steady.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #7.5 at 35 yards or less. Swing through the bird and keep the gun moving.
Shoot north only, with no house or field beyond the bird.

details.title: Technique: stay hidden
steps: Sit in shade with your back to the pine. Keep your face down.
Look up with your eyes, not your head.
Shoot the first bird that sets its wings and drops.

after: Tip: crows mobbing in the trees mean they found an owl or a hawk. Walk quietly toward the noise.

animals.name: Mourning dove
paragraphs: Doves pass between the pasture and the swamp pines in the first hour of light. Segment 2 runs Nov 7 to 28. Shooting hours start at legal light. HIP certification and a 3-shell plug are required.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #7.5 at 25 to 35 yards. Swing through the bird, then fire without stopping the gun.
Shoot only north, high enough that the shot clears the trees. Never toward the field SE.

after: Tip: a dove shot over the swamp falls in water or mud. Mark it before you shoot.

animals.name: Snipe
paragraphs: Snipe feed in the wet mud and shallows at the swamp edge. They flush with a harsh scaipe call and zig-zag. HIP certification and a 3-shell plug are required.

details.title: Technique: let it straighten
steps: Walk the mud margin slowly into the wind.
When a snipe flushes, wait. It zig-zags for 10 to 15 yards, then flies straight.
Shoot #7.5 once it levels out, north only.

after: Tip: look for small round probe holes in soft mud.

animals.name: Bear and bobcat
paragraphs: Awareness only. Bear season opens today, so you may hear other hunters. Give a bear space, talk out loud, and back away. Slugs are for defense only.

skill.title: Squirrel feed trees and nest reading
skill.principle: Squirrels are predictable because they eat in the same trees and sleep in the same nests. Find the food and the nests, and you know where to sit.

sections.title: Find the feed tree
steps: Walk slowly to the oaks, hickories, and holly in the loop pocket.
Look at the ground under each tree for cut hulls, nut shell bits, chewed acorn caps, and shredded holly berries.
Pick the tree with the biggest, freshest pile. Fresh pieces are bright and damp. Old ones are gray and dry.
Under pines, look for cone scales and cores. Sticky resin on the scales means fresh.

sections.title: Read the nests
steps: After the leaves drop, look up for round balls of leaves in forks, 20 to 40 feet high. Those are leaf nests.
A nest with green or fresh leaves is in use. A flattened gray nest is old.
Look for a hole in a trunk with a clean, chewed edge and bare bark below it. That is a den.
Mark nests near a feed tree. Squirrels travel between them at first light and late morning.

sections.title: Use it today
steps: From the seat, count the feed trees and nests you can see within 40 yards.
Watch the best feed tree in the sun from 7:15 on.
Do not shoot a squirrel in a nest tree toward the south. Only north, with a trunk or the ground behind.

details.title: Why it works in November
paragraphs: Nuts and cones are the main food now. Squirrels cache and re-eat them, so the same trees get used day after day. Leaf drop makes nests easy to see.

skill.checkpoint: Before you leave the seat, count the leaf nests and feed trees within 40 yards. Write down the number and which tree had the freshest pile. Send it with note:.

land.intro: You learn the land by reading what the squirrels leave behind.
steps: On the walk out, pick the 2 best feed trees you passed: biggest pile of fresh cuttings.
Pace each from the Junction and note the tree type if you know it.
Count the leaf nests you can see from the main trail between the Junction and the yard.
Send what you find with a note: message, for example: note: feed trees, 2 oaks, 40 and 70 paces from Junction, 5 nests.

safety: NEVER shoot south. The house is SW and the field is SE: no-shoot directions.
Every shot today goes between NW and E, with the ground or a trunk behind the animal.
Hunter orange hat and vest are required (Oct 17 to Jan 1). Deer gun season is still open for other hunters, and bear opens today.
Sky shots (dove, crow) only to the north, above the treeline.
Gusts to 15 mph can drop dead limbs. Do not sit under snags.
It is about 40F at walk-in. Wear layers you can open as it warms.

hunts.gaps: No hour-by-hour forecast was available for the hunt morning, so no hourly chart is shown. The forecast was issued Wednesday evening, and Saturday morning wind was not listed. The point used may not match the property exactly. Moonrise and moonset were not shown for Saturday. Migratory dates (dove, snipe, rails, ducks, woodcock, crow) and quail come from the state proclamation and season tables read tonight. Bag limits for squirrel, rabbit, raccoon, opossum, quail, and crow were not found. Legal light is sunrise minus 30 minutes.
